What is special/different about this method. We need to name it accordingly so it can be used for multiple variations if needed. cpld2 doesn't look reasonable and can't state its purpose.
The XO5-65T use a new implementation that introduces page-level CRC check and iamge hash verification during the update flow. I rename to lattice_xo5_65t instead of cpld2.

@Kyle.Hsieh@quantatw.com The way you explained looks like its just extra checks but no change in the way upgrade was actually performed, then why can't we fold this into existing lattic_xo5 flow and just add those extra checks based on specific xo5 type which is already available?
Is there a reason to add a completely new file just for this purpose?

I have folded the XO5-35T/65T support into the existing LatticeXO5CPLD class as suggested. By using an isTSeries flag, the specific command sequences for the T-Series are handled within the same flow, avoiding code duplication and the need for a new file.

Updated, I add the commit about XO5-25 testing on Santabarbara.
The current X05 file has become really big. Can you please move the X05 common code as a base class and then let the base model and T seres model extend from that.

I have refactored the XO5 CPLD driver to improve maintainability.

The monolithic LatticeXO5CPLD class has been split into a cleaner inheritance hierarchy:

LatticeXO5BaseCPLD: Handles common logic (e.g., base flow, utility interfaces).
LatticeXO5StandardCPLD: Implements Standard-specific logic.
LatticeXO5TSeriesCPLD: Implements T-Series specific logic (including version-specific CRC/Lock mechanisms).
Is this a new lock API. Is this needed on base model too?

The lockI2C API is indeed specific to the T-Series CPLD (SoftIP v2.0+). I will move it exclusively to LatticeXO5TSeriesCPLD, as the Standard model does not require this locking mechanism at all. This will help keep the base class lean and focused only on the common logic shared across all XO5 variants.
Is this lock needed on base model too?
Function toggleCrc16 exists in both SoftIP v1 and v2 within the T-Series. However, the lockI2C() requirement is specifically introduced in SoftIP v2.
Is this lock needed for base model too?
Function restoreHeader exists in both SoftIP v1 and v2 within the T-Series. However, the lockI2C() requirement is specifically introduced in SoftIP v2.

I dont see much difference between this code and one in X05 t series, please move this to base and provide the required args in constructor and add virtual functions which child classes can override, for example, lockI2C. I don't think we need to duplicate this code. Please follow similar pattern for other common APIs/code which can be moved to common base class.

Done. As suggested, I have moved the common logic (waitUntilReady) to the base class to remove duplication. The poll intervals are now passed via the base class constructor, and differences such as lockI2C are handled using overridden virtual functions (checkDeviceReady()).
